newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government faces confidence vote in Senate.
newsitem.headline: Italy government faces confidence vote in Senate.

text.p: The Italian government on Saturday called a confidence vote to ram a bill through the Senate on funding public works projects for millennium celebrations in Rome.

Environment Minister Edo Ronchi told the Senate the cabinet was forced to call a confidence vote because the bill needed to be passed quickly and there was not enough time to address numerous amendments.
The deadline for the bill's approval is Sunday.
Senate speaker Nicola Mancino, after meeting party leaders to discuss the matter, said the upper house would reconvene for opening comments at 1130 GMT and vote shortly afterwards.

The bill, which was approved by the lower house Chamber of Deputies on Friday, allocates 3.5 trillion lire ($2.3 billion) for public works projects to prepare the Italian capital for the end-of-the-century celebrations.
The city of Rome and the Vatican are gearing up for a huge influx of visitors in the year 2000, which Pope John Paul has declared a holy year, or jubilee.

Ronchi said that because of "the international importance" of the jubilee and the numerous amendments "which would not allow the bill to be approved by the scheduled deadline, the government calls a confidence vote".
The vote is the latest of several confidence votes the government has used to push legislation through parliament.

On Wednesday, the government won a confidence vote in the Senate to sweep aside opposition amendments and filibustering blocking passage of the 1997 budget, which must be passed into law by a year-end deadline.
